alerts.reason: June net sales fell 1.6%. Lower volume cost $9.38 million, roughly 3.9% of prior-year quarterly sales, while price increases added $2.44 million (A, C). I expect pricing to keep the September decline under 5%, with further volume losses pushing the December decline to at least 5%.

First-half revenue rose $31 million despite a $5 million June-quarter decline, implying a $36 million March-quarter gain. June revenue was down just 0.8% year over year (A). With oil and gas prices falling 10.0% and 23.1% sequentially (D), I expect customer demand to weaken gradually enough for revenue growth to stay above -5% in September and cross that threshold in December.

June revenue fell about 2.8% to $6.9 billion. IET growth of $0.2 billion offset half of a $0.4 billion OFSE decline that spanned North America and international markets (A–C). I expect IET growth to keep the September decline under 5%, then lower OFSE volume (D) to push the December decline to at least 5%.

June net sales fell 4.4%, but the order backlog fell 28.3% year over year to about $381 million (A–C). I expect existing orders to keep September sales growth above -5%, then the smaller backlog to push the December sales decline to at least 5% as orders convert to shipments.

June consolidated net sales fell 3.7%, just 1.3 percentage points short of a 5% decline (A). Volumes fell across geographies, and pricing offset only part of the loss (B, C). I expect pricing to keep the September decline under 5%, with continued volume pressure tipping reported sales to a decline of at least 5% in December.

Total net revenue fell 2% in both June and the first half despite 15% June growth in subscription and services revenue (A, B). Lower bitcoin trading volume outweighed the benefit of higher bitcoin prices (D). I expect services growth to keep September above -5%, with further trading-volume weakness pushing December total revenue growth to -5% or lower.

Revenue growth slowed from about 15.0% in March, derived from the half-year totals, to 9.1% in June (A). The filing attributes a $6.7 million inventory increase to lower demand (B). I expect revenue growth to remain above -5% in September, with weaker demand and accumulated inventory weighing on shipments enough for a decline of at least 5% in December.

June operating revenue fell 1.0%. Stable One-Way Truckload volumes extended into early September-quarter trading, but some fleet growth served temporary customer needs (A–C). I expect that work to keep the September revenue decline under 5%, then its expiration to deepen the December decline to at least 5%.
